headline: Proposed ordinance barring standing on narrow medians at high-risk intersections, presented by mayor and city staff.
summary: The mayor proposed lowering the width limit from 60 inches to 30 inches or less, which staff said would cover about seven intersections. Staff expect warnings and education first, with fines for repeat violators. Staff will look at the proposal in December and bring it back in January for possible action. The committee also unanimously voted to pursue state legislation on speed limits on roads where most fatalities and serious incidents happen.
decisions: Approved unanimously a motion to pursue potential state legislation on speed limits, focusing on roads with the most fatalities and bad incidents.
discussion: Median standing ordinance: Members raised concerns that crash data does not directly link time on a median to injuries, and that the public may call it a panhandling bill. The mayor said the goal is to move people out of risky spaces, not to jail them.
Services instead of fines: The mayor said people removed from medians could be referred to social services or a work group instead of being fined. Staff will explore job and mental health options.

Speed limit setting: A Public Works engineer estimated about 6,000 staff hours and about $750,000 to post about 1400 signs on about 400 townways. A public speaker said state speed rules are not working and asked for a citywide maximum of 25 miles per hour.

Commercial Street pilot: A regional planning group reported that the pilot, installed in late July, had no injury or fatal crashes in its stretch, and the pedestrian yield rate rose to 75.4%. The final report is expected in mid-December, and staff will decide whether to keep the painted features, pending state DOT approval.
Vision Zero updates: Staff reported three fatalities so far in 2026, compared with five last year, and crashes roughly on par with 2025. A Public Works lighting audit report is due in January.

decision_evidence.quote: So I would love to make a motion to pursue potential legislative changes on speed limits with the emphasis on roads where the majority of fatalities and bad incidents happen. ... Please let the record note that it was a unanimous vote decision.

decision_titles: Pursuing state legislation on speed limits
